system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: GCP
G2: Azure
G3: Istio/Linkerd in production
G4: CKAD (expired)
G5: line management

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing Istio or service mesh because SRE ads ask for it
T2: Listing CKAD
T3: Claiming GCP/Azure for multi-cloud ads
T4: Claiming people management / Engineering Manager
T5: Over-crediting Backstage plugin development
T6: Old cover letter is to her current employer and says she is at Brightwater

# OUTPUT 1: CV
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Site Reliability / Platform Engineer
nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior infrastructure engineer with 10 years of experience, including 6 years running Kubernetes
platforms on AWS. Technical lead experienced in cloud infrastructure design and operation, Terraform
infrastructure-as-code, and self-service platforms that help backend developers deploy and operate
services. Delivered measurable improvements in deployment speed, reliability and infrastructure cost
through GitOps, observability, SLOs and incident management.
EXPERIENCE
Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Apr 2022 - present
• Technical lead of a 5-person platform team, running an AWS EKS platform spanning 8 clusters,
approximately 350 services and 3 regions.
• Built an internal developer platform with service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane-based
self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3; reduced time from new service to production from
approximately 2 weeks to under 1 day.
• Introduced SLOs and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, reducing weekly on-call pages
by approximately 60%.
• Moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.
• Served in the incident commander rotation and wrote the incident and post-mortem process.
Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Jan 2019 - Mar 2022
• Operated AWS backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS and subsequently EKS for games with up to
1.2 million daily active players.
• Managed all AWS infrastructure through Terraform, with approximately 40 modules and Atlantis for
pull-request-based plan and apply workflows.
• Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability
stack.
• Used k6 for pre-launch load testing and carried out launch-day capacity planning.
Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Jul 2016 - Dec 2018
• Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration
management.
• Automated operations with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS, EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane, Puppet, GitHub Actions
Containers and deployment: Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Karpenter, GitOps
Observability and reliability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs,
error budgets, incident management, k6, capacity planning
Programming and systems: Go, Python, Bash, Linux
CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) - 2021, renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional - 2023
EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016
LANGUAGES
English (native), Urdu (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example
Corvale Mobility
Hiring Team
Application: Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor - Fleet Connectivity
Dear Hiring Team,
Corvale’s fleet connectivity project calls for cloud infrastructure that can move from initial
architecture to reliable production operation. I bring 10 years of infrastructure experience,
including 6 years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and currently lead a 5-person
platform team. My experience building self-service infrastructure, operating backend platforms
and improving observability provides a strong foundation for supporting the cloud side of your
new train fleet.
At Tallybrook, I run an EKS platform spanning 8 clusters, approximately 350 services and 3
regions. I built an internal developer platform combining service templates, Argo CD GitOps
and Crossplane-based provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3, reducing the time from new service to
production from approximately 2 weeks to under 1 day. This work closely matches your need to
support backend developers in deploying services that are straightforward to operate.
Introducing SLOs and error budgets for 20 critical services also reduced weekly on-call pages by
approximately 60%; I serve in the incident commander rotation and wrote our incident and
post-mortem process.
At Brightwater Games, I managed AWS infrastructure through approximately 40 Terraform
modules, with Atlantis providing plan and apply workflows on pull requests. I also replaced a
noisy monitoring setup with Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki, and used k6 load
testing to inform launch capacity planning for games serving up to 1.2 million daily active
players. These are directly relevant foundations for maintaining your infrastructure-as-code
repository and making the backend infrastructure supporting telemetry and alerting observable
and reliable.
Your brief combines early system design with responsibility for production outcomes. I would
bring technical leadership grounded in operating services at scale, practical Terraform
experience and a focus on making infrastructure usable for developers. I would welcome a
discussion about how this experience could contribute to Corvale’s fleet connectivity platform.
Yours sincerely,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
